questions.explanation:
1) No one lives above the floor where D lives. This implies that D lives on floor number 6.

2) K lives in a flat which is west of D's flat on the same floor. This implies that K lives on flat 1 of floor 6 which is the topmost floor and D lives in flat 2 on the same floor.

Note, now only 1 more person can live on floor 6.

3) There is a 2-floor gap where T and D live and both live on the same flat number. Here T lives on flat 2 of floor 3.

4) E and K are neighbors. So E must live in flat 2 on floor 6.

Now, the arrangement on floor 6 is complete.

5) There are 5 flats gap in between where E and U live. So U shares his flat with T in flat 2 on floor 3

6) F lives on an odd number floor and flat alone in his flat.

7) U and F live in the adjacent flat. This implies F lives in flat 1 on floor 3.

Now our arrangement on floor numbers 3 and 6 is complete.

Direction: In following question two conclusions have been given followed by 5 sets of possible Statements. You have to take the given Conclusions to be true even if they seem to be at variance with the commonly known facts and then decide for the given Conclusions logically follows from the which of the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Conclusion: Some T are Chair. No Cup is a P.

options.text: Statements: Some T are chair. All T are P. No Cup is T.
Statement: Some P are Chair. All P are T. No cup is T.
Statement: No P is Chair. Some T are P. All Cups are T.
Statement: No P is Chair. All T are P. Some Cups are T.

questions.explanation:
Conclusion:

I. Some T are Chair.

II. No Cup is a P

Statements: Some T are chair. All T are P. No Cup is T.

Some T are Chair→ True (As some T are chair)

No Cup is a P → False (There is a possibility of All cups are P. Hence, False)

Hence, above statements does not gives the result for the given conclusion.

Statement: Some P are Chair. All P are T. No cup is T.

Some T are Chair → True (All P are T and Some P are Chair. so, part of T that is P is also chair)

No Cup is a P → True ( All P are T. No cup is T. So, No cup is P)

Hence, above statements gives the result for the given conclusion.

No need to check further statements.

Hence, statement of option (2) will result in given conclusion.

Direction: In the following question, two conclusions have been given followed by sets of possible Statements. You have to take the given Conclusions to be true even if they seem to be at variance with the commonly known facts and then decide for the given Conclusions logically follows from the which of the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Conclusions: Some B are C.  Some M are not R.

options.text: Statements: All M are C. Some R are not C. Some M are B.
Statements: Some C are not R. All C are M. All M are B.
Statements: All C are R. No R are M. No M are B.
Statements: Some C are R. No R are M. Some M are B.

questions.explanation:
Conclusions:

I. Some B are C

II. Some M are not R 

Statement: All M are C. Some R are not C. Some M are B.

I. Some B are C →True (All M are C and Some M are B so, some B are definitely C)

II. Some M are not R →False (It is possible but not definite)

In above venn diagram conclusion II does not follow.

Hence, above statement will not result in given conclusion.

2) Statement: Some C are not R. All C are M. All M are B.

I. Some B are C →True (All C are M. All M are B. So, some B are definitely C)

II. Some M are not R →True (Some C are not R. All C are M. so, some M that are C are not R)

In above venn diagram conclusion I and II follows.

Hence, above statement will give result in given conclusion.

No need to check further.

Hence, Option 2 statement will result in given conclusion.

questions.text:
Direction: In the following question, a given question is followed by information in two statements. You have to find out the data in which statement (s) is sufficient to answer the question and mark your answer accordingly.

There is a family of seven members. How is G related to Q?

Statement I: Q is the brother of W, who is married to his wife Z. P is married to Q. D is the niece of W, who has one son and one daughter. G and R are Cousins of D.

Statement II: W is the brother of Q, who is the husband of P. Z is the sister-in-law of Q, whose daughter is D. R is the niece of Q and G is the nephew of Q.

options.text: The data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question
The data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question
The data either in statement I alone or in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question
The data in both statements I and II together is not sufficient to answer the question
The data in both statements I and II together is necessary to answer the question

questions.explanation:
According to the given information,

Total family members: Seven

Statement I: Q is the brother of W, who is married to his wife Z. P is married to Q. D is the niece of W, who has one son and one daughter. G and R are Cousins of D.

1. Q is the brother of W, who is married to his wife Z.

2. P is married to Q.

3. D is the niece of W, who has one son and one daughter.

4. G and R are Cousins of D.

Here the gender of G can't be determined. Hence Statement I alone is not sufficient to find how is G related to Q.

Statement II: W is the brother of Q, who is the husband of P. Z is the sister-in-law of Q, whose daughter is D. R is the niece of Q and G is the nephew of Q.

1. W is the brother of Q, who is the husband of P.

2. Z is the sister-in-law of Q, whose daughter is D.

3. R is the niece of Q and G is the nephew of Q.

Therefore, G is the nephew of Q.

Hence, The data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

questions.text: Who is the class teacher of 5<sup>th</sup> grade?
questions.explanation:
1) B is sitting third to the right of the class teacher of 3rd class.

2) C is sitting second to the right of B.

(Implies, if B is sitting on the edge then C is also sitting on the edge or if B is sitting on the corner then C is also sitting on the corner.)

3) The person sitting to the immediate right of C is sitting on the corner seat.

(Implies, B is also sitting on the edge. Now according to statement 1, we can randomly place the class teacher of the 3rd class on any corner seat and then we can place B and C accordingly.)

4) E is an immediate neighbour of C and he is sitting opposite the class teacher of 7th grade.

(It is only possible if we place E to the immediate right of C. It further implies that the teacher sitting to the immediate left of B teaches 7th grade.)

5) A is sitting third to the right of G who is an immediate neighbour of B.

(We cannot place G to the immediate left of B as C is sitting third to the right of that seat, implies, G is sitting to the immediate right of B and A is sitting to the immediate left of E.)

6) H is not sitting on any of the edges and he teaches the class that us three years junior to G’s class.

(Implies, H is sitting on one of the corner seats. Also, as he teaches a class that is 3 years junior to G’s class, implies, he is not sitting to the immediate left of B because the teacher on that seat is the class teacher of 7th grade. Hence, H is sitting opposite G and it means that H is the class teacher of 3rd grade. It also implies that G is the class teacher of 6th grade.)

7) A teaches the class that is 6 years senior to D’s class.

(Implies, D is the class teacher of either class 1 or 2. It further implies that D is sitting to the immediate right of H as there are only two seats left and D can’t be sitting to the immediate left of B as the teacher on that seat teaches 7th grade. Also, as A is not the class teacher of 7th grade, implies, D is the class teacher of 2nd grade and A is the class teacher of 8th grade. Also, now that only one teacher is left to be placed, we can place F to the immediate left of B as it is the only seat left.)

8) B teaches the class that is one year senior to E’s class.

(Three classes are left to be mapped at this moment i.e. class 1, 4, and 5. Clearly, it means that B is the class teacher of 5th class and E is the class teacher of the 4th class. Also, now that only one class is left to be mapped, we can say that C is the class teacher of 1st class as it is the only possibility.)

Clearly, B is the class teacher of 5th grade.
